issue.title: Erratic behavior in selectbox when the index parameter is not a constant

issue.body:
# Summary

According to the documentation, the [selectbox](https://docs.streamlit.io/en/latest/api.html#streamlit.selectbox)'s index parameter provides the preselected option on first render. When the selectbox is already rendered but the index parameter is changed, the selection changes but it shouldn't change.

# Steps to reproduce

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-1532)

1. Execute the following streamlit application:

```
import streamlit as st
options = ['zero', 'one', 'two', 'three']
first = st.selectbox('selectbox 1', options, index=2)
second = st.selectbox('selectbox 2', options, index=options.index(first))
```

2. Open the page in the browser.

3. Select boxes "selectbox 1" and "selectbox 2" should be shown, both with option "two" selected.

4. Change the selection in "selectbox 1". The selection in "selectbox 2" will also change, but it shouldn't change.

## Expected behavior:

"selectbox 2" should not copy "selectbox 1".

## Actual behavior:

"selectbox 2" copies "selectbox 1".

## Is this a regression?

no

# Debug info

- Streamlit version: 0.60.0
- Python version: 3.7.5
- Using virtualenv
- OS version: Windows 10
- Browser version: Google Chrome 83.0.4103.61 (Official Build) (64-bit)

# Additional information

I've found the possible cause and a solution. According to the following lines in [DeltaGenerator.py](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/c6919ba8fd64bf03cc4da9efaa09b55cc0fa47dd/lib/streamlit/DeltaGenerator.py#L170), it seems that the element hash changes when the index parameter is updated and so does the widget id.
```
def _set_widget_id(widget_type, element, user_key=None):
    element_hash = hash(element.SerializeToString())
    if user_key is not None:
        widget_id = "%s-%s" % (user_key, element_hash)
    else:
        widget_id = "%s" % element_hash
```
In order to provide the desired behavior, the variable widget_id should not change if the index parameter changes. One simple solution is redefining how the parameter user_key is used. The following code patches the described behavior:

```
def _set_widget_id(widget_type, element, user_key=None):
    element_hash = hash(element.SerializeToString())
    if user_key is not None:
        widget_id = "%s" % user_key
    else:
        widget_id = "%s" % element_hash
```

Then the key parameter has to be provided to "selectbox 2" in the streamlit application:

```
import streamlit as st
options = ['zero', 'one', 'two', 'three']
first = st.selectbox('selectbox 1', options, index=2)
second = st.selectbox('selectbox 2', options, index=options.index(first), key='second_selectbox')
```

The validity of this solution depends on the use cases defined for the user_key parameter, but for the moment I haven't observed any side effects.

issue.title: Fix text input reverting value

repository.name: streamlit
repository.description: Streamlit — A faster way to build and share data apps.

issue.body:
Fixes https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/678
Fixes https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1532

The issue is that our widget IDs are generated by hashing the contents of the widget proto. This includes the `.default` field. So when the user passes a new value to `st.text_input(value=...)`, the widget gets a new ID, and is no longer associated with its previous value in our widget state.

This fixes a general class of bugs wherein passing a changing value to `st.text_input` & co will change their widget "identity," resulting a wide range of unforeseen consequences.

Incidentally, the reason passing a `key` didn't solve anything was that even when a user key is passed, we still concatenate the widget hash onto it.
